family: The single total language defined in proof.md Chapter I, with all recursive and atomic algorithms supplied in supporting_proofs.md. Fix M=100 permanently. At actual length N<4 output zero. Otherwise choose the largest integer n>=1 with n+h(n)<=N, where h(n)=2*ceil(n^(3/50000))+1. Read the first h(n) bits as the lower coefficients of a monic degree-h(n) binary polynomial Q, the next n bits as payload x, and the remaining bits as padding y. Set base to zero if the explicit finite guard in Chapter I fails or Q is reducible. Otherwise evaluate the fixed reciprocal-parameter recursive challenge-response construction of supporting_proofs.md Chapter VIII on x over F_2[T]/Q(T), with the exact parameters, tie rules, and encoders in the proof. Output base XOR parity(y). All lengths and all bit strings are defined. Every header and padding bit counts in N. One fixed polynomial-time evaluator and the verifier that accepts exactly empty witnesses on inputs whose evaluator is one define the language at every length.
theorem: For this one fixed total language in P, hence in NP with witness bound zero, every exact circuit in the full pinned B2 model at actual input length N has at least 4*N-8*N^(1/100)-6*N^(3/50000)-23 gates for every sufficiently large integer N. Consequently the same family has at least 4*N-9*N^(1/100) gates for every sufficiently large integer N, and liminf over all integer lengths of C_B2(F_N)/N is at least 4. All sixteen binary truth tables, one output, arbitrary sharing and fan-out are covered. M and all algorithms remain fixed throughout the asymptotic quantifiers.
